title: Gamma and Theta: The Core Greeks Tradeoff
summary: Cards spanning gamma, theta, time-decay, and their structural relationship in options positions. Covers the gamma-theta tradeoff that underpins all short-vol strategies — collecting theta in exchange for gamma exposure — position-level greek aggregation at expiration, and how ATM options maximise both gamma and theta simultaneously.

title: Delta-Neutral Trading and Gamma Scalping
summary: The mechanics of maintaining delta neutrality and extracting realised-vol P&L through gamma scalping. Covers delta-hedge rebalancing discipline, how a long-gamma position profits when realised vol exceeds implied, the costs of over-hedging, and the vol-trading edge that emerges from active delta management across multiple books.

title: Delta and Moneyness: Directional Sensitivity
summary: Delta as the primary measure of directional exposure and a probability-of-expiring-ITM proxy. Covers ATM, ITM, and OTM moneyness definitions, intrinsic vs. extrinsic value decomposition, how delta evolves with spot price, and the relationship between delta and the N(d1) term in BSM.

title: Rho, Interest Rates, Dividends, and Forward Pricing
summary: The sensitivity of option prices to interest rates and dividends. Covers rho as a greek, the role of carry in put-call parity, how dividends lower call prices and raise put prices, LEAPS sensitivity to long-dated interest rates, and forward price mechanics as the risk-neutral anchor for option pricing.

title: Synthetic Positions and Put-Call Parity
summary: Constructing synthetic equivalents of stock and option positions using put-call parity. Covers synthetic long stock (long call + short put), synthetic short stock (short call + long put), call-put equivalences, and the arbitrage relationships that enforce these identities — the structural glue binding the options market.

title: Multi-Leg Volatility Strategies: Straddles, Strangles, Butterflies, and Condors
summary: The mechanics and P&L profiles of the core premium-selling structures. Covers straddles and strangles as pure volatility plays with unlimited loss, butterflies and condors as defined-risk alternatives, the P&L distribution characteristics of each, and how these structures express different views on realised vol magnitude and range.

title: Vega and Implied Volatility: The Earnings Vol Crush
summary: Vega as the sensitivity to implied volatility changes, with particular focus on event-driven IV dynamics. Covers vol inflation ahead of earnings announcements, the mechanics of the IV crush post-announcement as uncertainty resolves, vega-weighted position sizing, and how to use volatility charts to identify elevated premium opportunities.

title: Volatility Term Structure: Contango, Backwardation, and Calendar Spreads
summary: The shape and dynamics of the implied volatility term structure across expiration dates. Covers VIX futures contango as a structural drag on long-vol ETPs, calendar spread construction to exploit term structure slope, GARCH-based forward vol forecasting, and regime shifts between contango (normal) and backwardation (crisis) states.

title: Portfolio-Level Greek Risk Management
summary: A holistic framework for managing aggregate greek exposure across a multi-position portfolio. Covers delta/gamma aggregation across positions, greek limits as risk boundaries, the role of vega in portfolio-level vol exposure, and the trading philosophy and discipline required to sustain a systematic vol-selling operation through drawdowns.

title: Implied Volatility Mean Reversion and Variance Swaps
summary: The statistical behaviour of implied volatility as a mean-reverting process. Covers VIX mean reversion dynamics and historical reversion speed, model-free variance swap replication as a purer vol measure than ATM IV, the variance risk premium embedded in options prices, and practical timing implications for entering short-vol positions.

title: Box Spreads and Interest Rate Arbitrage
summary: Using box spreads as synthetic loans and risk-free interest rate arbitrage vehicles. Covers long-box and short-box construction, their financing economics, how market makers use box spreads to exploit rate differentials between brokers, and why a short-box trade is economically equivalent to borrowing at the risk-free rate.

title: Historical vs. Implied Volatility: Forecasting and the Variance Premium
summary: The relationship between historical realised volatility and implied volatility as a forward estimate. Covers volatility forecasting methods (GARCH, rolling HV), the persistent variance premium that makes options systematically overpriced, how IV and HV diverge across regimes, and how this gap drives the core edge in options selling strategies.

title: Theta-Vega Interaction in OTM Options
summary: How time decay and vega interact specifically in out-of-the-money options. Covers the non-linear theta accumulation profile for short OTM positions, vega sensitivity at different strikes relative to ATM, and the gamma-theta tradeoff at the wings where both are lower but so is the hedge cost — the structural basis for strangle and condor strategies.

title: Volatility Skew and Structural OTM Put Premium
summary: The persistent skew in the implied volatility surface driven by structural insurance demand for downside protection. Covers risk-reversal trading to harvest the skew, the higher IV embedded in OTM puts versus OTM calls, covered-call writing as a skew-harvesting strategy, and why the skew persists as a structural rather than temporary pricing anomaly.

title: Market Maker Edge and Theoretical Value
summary: How market makers define and extract edge relative to theoretical option value. Covers bid-ask spread as compensation for gamma risk, delta-neutral pricing anchors, the difference between risk-neutral model value and real-world trading edge, and the competitive dynamics that compress spreads over time.

title: Kelly Criterion and Fractional Position Sizing
summary: Optimal position sizing using the Kelly criterion and its fractional variants for vol strategies. Covers full-Kelly growth maximisation and its brutal drawdown profile, the practical advantages of half-Kelly (75% growth rate at 25% variance cost), and how to calibrate bet size to measured edge and outcome variance in options strategies.

title: High-Efficiency Volatility Estimators: Parkinson, Garman-Klass, Rogers-Satchell
summary: Historical volatility estimators that exploit OHLC data to achieve far higher efficiency than close-to-close returns. Covers Parkinson's range-based estimator (4.9× efficiency), Garman-Klass (7.4× efficiency), and Rogers-Satchell's drift-adjustment. Knowing which estimator to use for a given data regime is critical to accurate vol measurement.

title: Conversions and Reversals: Operational Put-Call Parity Arbitrage
summary: Conversion and reversal structures as operational put-call parity arbitrage used by market makers. Covers how conversions (long put + short call + long stock) and reversals (short put + long call + short stock) lock in risk-free profits when parity is violated, their financing mechanics, and why they are rare but important in practice.

title: Black-Scholes-Merton Assumptions and Their Violations
summary: The idealising assumptions of Black-Scholes-Merton and how each fails in real markets. Covers log-normal returns vs. observed fat tails, continuous hedging impossibility and transaction costs, constant volatility vs. the smile, and how these violations explain observed skew, kurtosis risk premia, and the limits of BSM as a pricing tool vs. a quoting convention.

title: Option Payoff Profiles and P&L Diagrams
summary: The foundational payoff structures of long and short calls and puts at expiration. Covers payoff diagrams that decompose premium paid/received from intrinsic value, the asymmetric risk-reward of long vs. short positions, and how these building blocks combine into the multi-leg structures covered across multiple books in this knowledge base.

title: Vertical Spreads: Defined-Risk Directional Structures
summary: Bull call spreads, bear put spreads, and bear call spreads as defined-risk alternatives to naked directional options. Covers strike selection mechanics, maximum profit and loss profiles, the tradeoff between lower premium cost and capped upside, and how vertical spreads are used to express a directional view with contained downside.

title: Straddle Strategies: Long and Short Volatility Expressions
summary: The straddle as the purest expression of a pure volatility view, divorced from direction. Covers long straddle construction and its breakeven range, short straddle as premium collection with unlimited risk, the dominant role of vega in P&L sensitivity, and when each side of the trade has positive expected value.

title: Position-Level Greek Risk in Spread Structures
summary: How greek exposure aggregates across a spread position, with focus on sign changes and non-linear risk. Covers gamma sign-flip in bull call spreads near the short strike — where the position transitions from long-gamma to short-gamma — combined delta and vega exposure, and position-level greek limits as practical risk controls.

title: Expiration Risk: Pin Risk, Assignment, and Automatic Exercise
summary: The operational and market risks that arise near option expiration. Covers pin risk when the underlying settles near a strike, early assignment risk for short American options, automatic exercise mechanics for in-the-money options, and the practical steps market makers and traders take to manage unexpected delta exposure at expiration.
